title: A method to measure the partitioning coefficient of volatile organic compounds in nanoparticles
author: Rao, Ahn, et al.

steps.title: Assemble chamber and air supply
steps.instruction: Fabricate the aluminum environmental chamber (0.3 m diameter, 0.1 m height) with a removable lid secured by 12 Allen screws and an O‑ring for sealing. Place the chamber inside a temperature‑controlled cabinet (CEO932). Connect compressed house air at 240 kPa, pass it through a hydrocarbon trap (BHT‑4, Agilent) and a HEPA filter (83690H, Pall) to provide clean, particle‑free air for all streams.

steps.title: Generate and set flow streams
steps.instruction: Create three separate streams (diluted 1,2‑DCB, aerosol, humid air) and deliver them to the chamber at the prescribed flow rates, pressures, and relative humidity.

substeps.instruction: Diluted 1,2‑DCB: Place a 2‑mL vial containing 1 mL pure 1,2‑DCB in a Precision Standard Gas Generator (491M‑B, KIN‑TEC). Vapor effuses through a 400‑µm deactivated glass capillary and is diluted with particle‑free air. Adjust the air flow to 45 mL min⁻¹, yielding a diluted 1,2‑DCB concentration of 17 ± 1 ppbv.

Aerosol: Atomize a 250 ppm (NH₄)₂SO₄ solution using an atomizer (TSI3076) at 2.5 L min⁻¹ house air and 207 kPa. Pass the aerosol through a diffusion dryer (Model 3062, TSI) containing silica. Use a needle valve (instead of an MFC) to set the aerosol flow to 100 mL min⁻¹ into the chamber, minimizing size fluctuations.

Humid air: Produce wet air with two 20‑gallon water saturators in series. Insert an empty 1‑L glass container between the saturators and the MFC to protect the MFC from condensation. Set wet‑air flow to 155 mL min⁻¹; combine with the dry‑air stream to obtain a total flow of 300 mL min⁻¹ (45 + 100 + 155) and a chamber RH of 20 % as measured by a USBQTENKI‑T‑RH‑CC2 probe (Dracal). All flow rates are controlled by a LabVIEW program interfaced with mass‑flow controllers (FC‑280, Tylan).

Sampling stream: Pull chamber air with a vacuum pump (Model 10473, EMS) at 300 mL min⁻¹ through a Tenax‑packed thermal‑desorption (TD) tube (Markes). Upstream of the TD tube place two carbon denuders (ADI‑DEN2, Aerosol Dynamics) in series. Condition each denuder at 135 °C for 10 h using high‑purity N₂ (>99.999 %) at 150 mL min⁻¹ before sampling. The denuders (20 cm length, ~500 channels, ~700 m² g⁻¹ surface area) remove gas‑phase 1,2‑DCB while allowing >90 % of aerosols to pass.

steps.title: Configure LabVIEW and MFC control
steps.instruction: Load the custom LabVIEW virtual instrument, connect it to all MFCs and the RH probe, and program the desired flow rates and RH set‑point (20 %). Enable the virtual PID controller for RH feedback. Verify communication with each device before proceeding.

steps.title: Set up TD‑GC/MS system
steps.instruction: Configure the thermal desorber, gas chromatograph, and mass spectrometer with the parameters listed below, and load the internal standard onto each TD tube for quality control.

substeps.instruction: Thermal desorber: primary desorption valve 225 °C, tube temperature 225 °C, transfer line 250 °C, trap temperature ramp from –30 °C to 300 °C at 40 °C s⁻¹, purge time 1 min, desorption time 5 min, trap hold 7 min, He carrier (99.999 %) at 50 mL min⁻¹, inlet split flow 20 mL min⁻¹, outlet split flow 20 mL min⁻¹, column pressure 12 psi.

GC column: Agilent DB‑5ms, 30 m × 0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm film, 5 % phenyl‑methylpolysiloxane. Column flow 1 mL min⁻¹ (He). Oven program: 50 °C (0.5 min), ramp 25 °C min⁻¹ to 100 °C, then to 180 °C, hold 1 min.

MS: Electron ionization 70 eV, source temperature 200 °C, trap emission 100 V, repeller 1.0 V, lens voltages 1, 25, 55 V, filament current 0.07 A, CLM resolution 8.0, HM resolution 12.5, ion energy 2.5 eV (ramp 1.5 V), multiplier 1650 V, SIM mode monitoring m/z 111 and 146 for 1,2‑DCB, and m/z 78, 115, 152 for deuterated 1,2‑DCB‑d₄ (internal standard). Dwell time 0.05 s, inter‑channel delay 0.05 s, retention window 4.3–5 min, solvent delay 4 min.
Internal standard: inject 1 µL of 500 ppb 1,2‑DCB‑d₄ onto each TD tube before analysis.

steps.title: Generate calibration curve
steps.instruction: Prepare standards of 0, 25, 50, 100, and 200 ppb 1,2‑DCB in methanol (2‑mL amber GC vials), add 500 ppb 1,2‑DCB‑d₄ to each, inject 1 µL onto clean TD tubes, analyze by TD‑GC/MS, and plot the peak‑area ratio (ADCB/AIS) versus concentration to obtain a linear calibration (slope = 0.0025, SD = 0.0108). The limit of detection is 13 pg (3 × SD / slope).

steps.title: Pre‑condition TD tube before sampling
steps.instruction: Heat the Tenax TD tube at 330 °C for 20 min while flowing ultrapure N₂ at 50 mL min⁻¹. After cooling, re‑analyze the tube in the TD‑GC/MS system to confirm absence of 1,2‑DCB.

steps.title: Equilibrate system
steps.instruction: Run the three streams (45 mL min⁻¹ DCB, 100 mL min⁻¹ aerosol, 155 mL min⁻¹ wet air) continuously for at least 2 h at the target temperature (15 °C or 35 °C) and 20 % RH. Monitor aerosol size, TSP, and gas‑phase 1,2‑DCB until they reach steady values (as shown in Fig. 7).

steps.title: Measure gas‑phase concentration (Cig)
steps.instruction: Sample the chamber outlet *before* the denuders with a Tenax TD tube at 25 mL min⁻¹ for 0.5 min (sample volume V = 12.5 mL). Desorb and quantify 1,2‑DCB by TD‑GC/MS. Compute Cig = mig / V (µg m⁻³, ppb), where mig is the mass captured on the TD tube. Example result: Cig = 2.57 ± 0.12 ppb.

steps.title: Measure aerosol‑phase concentration (Cip)
steps.instruction: Sample the chamber outlet *after* the denuders for 24 h at 300 mL min⁻¹ (sampling volume V = 0.432 m³). Desorb the TD tube and quantify 1,2‑DCB. Subtract the residual gas‑phase mass measured in a control test without aerosol (51 ± 32 pg) to obtain mip. Compute Cip = mip / V (µg m⁻³, ppb).

steps.title: Measure total suspended particulate mass (TSP)
steps.instruction: Replace the 1,2‑DCB stream with clean house air, set RH to the minimum achievable (~4 %). Connect the chamber outlet to an Electrostatic Classifier (Model 3082, TSI) and a Condensation Particle Counter (Model 3775, TSI) at 300 mL min⁻¹. Record TSP, median diameter, and number concentration for at least five replicates. Example average: TSP = 1186 ± 92 µg m⁻³, median diameter = 107 ± 1 nm, number concentration = (4.66 ± 0.34) × 10⁵ cm⁻³.

steps.title: Determine deposition efficiencies
steps.instruction: At 20 % RH, measure aerosol properties at three locations: chamber outlet, after the denuders, and after the TD tube. Calculate deposition efficiency as 1 – (TSP downstream / TSP upstream). Reported values: ~9 % loss in denuders, 86 % captured by TD tube, overall retention 78 % (dry aerosol TSP ≈ 930 µg m⁻³).

steps.title: Calculate partition coefficient (Kip)
steps.instruction: Use Eq. (1): Kip = Cip / (Cig × TSP). Insert the measured Cig, Cip, and dry‑aerosol TSP to obtain Kip (units m³ µg⁻¹). Example results: 2.80 ± 0.40 × 10⁻¹⁰ m³ µg⁻¹ at 15 °C and 3.34 ± 0.59 × 10⁻¹⁰ m³ µg⁻¹ at 35 °C. Convert to mass of 1,2‑DCB per µg aerosol (0.72–0.85 pg µg⁻¹).
